title: Real-world Integration Latency Lab Protocol
author: Elena Park
body:
Summary:
This document defines the lab protocol for measuring and validating real-world end-to-end latency for Redwood's serving runtime when integrated with typical customer stacks. The goal is reproducible, comparable results across experiments and a clear path from measurement to mitigation and runbook updates. This protocol covers test harness configuration, kernel scheduling knobs to exercise, profiling instrumentation, benchmark metrics, acceptance gates, triage steps, and release checklist items.

Why this exists:
- Many microbenchmarks do not expose systemic latency sources (networking, pre/post-processing, SDK client behavior, model-variant switching).
- Product teams need a repeatable integration workflow to validate latency budgets before shipping model variants or scheduler changes.
- Oncall and SRE require deterministic steps to reproduce customer-facing tail latency and to collect the exact traces needed for root-cause analysis.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Hosted API path, Dedicated pools (single-tenant), and Private deployment reference config. Includes kernel and scheduler toggle exercises, KV cache warmup patterns, and cross-service tracing.
- Non-goal: Microkernel engineering (kernel code changes should be validated in the kernel lab and referenced here).

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / Benchmarking (Elena Park)
- SRE escalation lead: Arjun Patel
- Profiling & Observability contact: Sofia Martinez
- Release engineering reviewer: Priya Singh

High-level success criteria (sample SLOs for lab runs):
1) Median p95-p99 delta under controlled synthetic load must be < 1.5x baseline.
2) 99th percentile absolute latency (end-to-end, client-observed) must be < 250 ms for small prompt workloads (<= 128 tokens) on Dedicated rtx-llama-8 profile.
3) No more than 5% of requests may observe > 300 ms extra jitter after model-variant swap during a 30-minute canary exercise.

Test environment matrix (table):
- Hardware: rtx-llama-8, a100-40, a800-64 configurations
- Deployment modes: hosted-api (eu-west1), dedicated-small (8-GPU pool), private-onprem (1-rack)
- Network: local-test VLAN, simulated 50 ms cross-region latency, baseline intra-region
- Client SDK: python-sdk v2.8, go-sdk v1.5

(Represented as a human-readable table in the lab runbook):
| axis | options |
|------|---------|
| hardware | rtx-llama-8, a100-40, a800-64 |
| deployment | hosted-api, dedicated-small, private-onprem |
| network profile | intra-region (10ms), cross-region (50ms), congested (100ms +- 20ms jitter) |
| client load | single-request steady, sustained qps, bursty microbursts (10x baseline) |

Instrumentation and data to collect (mandatory):
- Client-side: request timestamp, sdk version, client region, request size, prompt token count, retry count.
- Edge: ingress latency, TLS handshake times, proxy queue depth.
- Runtime: dispatch latency, kernel selection, batch size, kernel exec time, KV cache hit/miss, memory pressure events.
- Kernel traces: per-kernel wall time, tensor upload/download durations, kernel queuing time, accelerator telemetry (SM utilization, temperature, power).
- Tracing: full distributed trace with unique run_id; ensure trace IDs propagate through edge -> router -> runtime -> kernel.
- Aggregates: per-route p50/p90/p95/p99, concurrency histogram, CPU/GPU tail utilization, retry/backpressure counts.

Profiling playbook integration steps:
1) Baseline capture: run 30 minutes of steady-state single-request-to-queue traffic at 1x production QPS. Collect lightweight traces (1/100 sampling) plus full traces for 1 minute every 5 minutes.
2) Microburst capture: inject 10x QPS for 60s bursts every 10 minutes. Use high-frequency sampling (1/10) during bursts.
3) Model swap: trigger a canary model-variant swap (v1 -> v1-quantized) and capture traces for 30 minutes post-swap with 100% sampling.
4) Kernel-change simulation: toggle scheduler gating parameter (kernel_credit_floor) to stress preemption and run a 15-minute stress profile.
5) KV warm/cold runs: run identical prompts with cold KV (restart runtime between runs) and warm KV (run warmup with 1000 unique requests).

Procedure: running a lab experiment (numbered checklist)
1. Reserve lab environment: use the bench-run booking service (benchctl reserve --env=<env-name> --hours=3). Document reservation id.
2. Deploy benchmark artifacts: push canary model to bench registry and pin runtime image to stable-<sha>.
3. Configure experiment: edit run_config.yaml (see sample below) and upload to bench-run.
4. Start instrumentation collectors: start jaeger, perf-collector, nvtop-exporter, and bench-metrics-shipper. Confirm metrics ingestion in metrics-redwood/baseline-run.
5. Execute baseline and perturbations following the profile above.
6. Export artifacts: traces (JSON), aggregates (CSV), kernel histograms (parquet), and nvml snapshots (tar.gz). Attach to the bench-run ticket.
7. Annotate findings: fill the experiment-summary template and link to related issues.
8. Close reservation and notify reviewers.

Sample run_config.yaml (literal block):
---
run_id: rw-latency-experiment-2026-08
hardware: rtx-llama-8
deployment: dedicated-small
client: python-sdk-2.8
qps_profile: |
  - step: steady
    qps: 50
    duration: 1800
  - step: burst
    qps: 500
    duration: 60
  - step: cooldown
    qps: 50
    duration: 600
sampling: 
  steady: 1/100
  burst: 1/10
  post_swap: 1/1
---

Acceptance gates and triage thresholds:
- Gate A (pre-merge): No p99 regression > 2x baseline on median of 3 independent runs.
- Gate B (canary): < 1% increase in client-visible request failures and p99 within SLO.
- Gate C (release): 3-run streak of passing Gate A and one canary pass after scheduler toggle.

If a gate fails run the triage checklist: (short steps)
1) Re-run the exact experiment with debug sampling enabled (100% traces for 5 minutes).
2) Correlate traces with kernel histograms and NVML snapshots by run_id.
3) Check for scheduler backpressure signals (kernel_credit_balance < 0), dispatcher queue depth > 90th percentile, or KV eviction storms.
4) Narrow to layer (network, dispatch, kernel) and open a priority P0 investigation ticket with attached artifacts.

Known issues to watch for during runs (operational guidance):
- Intermittent nvlink retransmits when multiple A100s are under microburst stress: remediate by toggling cross-gpu coalescing off and retest.
- SDK client-side exponential backoff misconfiguration: ensure client max_retries=2 for lab runs.
- Kernel driver stutters manifested as 10-20ms spikes on p99: capture kernel logs and escalate to kernel-team with trace artifacts.

Kernel scheduling knobs exercised by this protocol:
- kernel_credit_floor: minimum credits to keep a kernel resident.
- preempt_grace_window_ms: time window before allowing preemption of running kernel slices.
- batch_slice_target_ms: target slice duration used by the batch-slicer.
- admission_watermark: soft queue threshold to trigger admission backpressure.

Release checklist tie-ins (before rolling runtime changes):
- Ensure three lab runs across the environment matrix pass acceptance gates.
- Document any scheduler knob changes in the release notes with exact config diffs.
- Attach representative traces and a short remediation playbook for SRE.

Runbook snippet for oncall (short, actionable):
- Symptom: customer complains of increased tail latency after rollout.
- Quick checks: verify canary-run_id in bench-run, check runtime dispatch queue depth, verify kernel_credit_balance and GPU utilization.
- Immediate mitigation: revert scheduler knob to previous value (idempotent config), scale up warm spare pool for 15 minutes, and notify release-owner.
- Collect: full traces for 10 minutes after mitigation and attach to ticket.

Post-experiment analysis and reporting template (bulleted):
- Experiment objective and hypothesis
- Environment and exact artifacts (images, model-sha, run_id)
- Key metrics: baseline p95/p99, post-change p95/p99, CPU/GPU tail util
- Notable traces and causal inference (short narrative)
- Recommended action: rollback, config tweak, kernel bug, or accept

Artifacts and storage policy:
- Store all collected traces and artifacts under s3://bench-archive/<run_id>/ with 90-day hot retention and 2-year cold archive.
- Sensitive data (customer prompts) must be redacted before upload following the data-management template.

Appendix A — Quick CLI snippets:
- Reserve environment: benchctl reserve --env=dedicated-small --hours=3
- Start collection: benchctl collect start --run_id=rw-latency-experiment-2026-08
- Upload artifacts: benchctl upload --run_id=rw-latency-experiment-2026-08 --path=./artifacts

Appendix B — Common troubleshooting queries (examples):
- Find runs with p99 > 300ms: SELECT run_id FROM bench_metrics WHERE metric='p99' AND value > 300 AND date >= '2026-01-01';
- Correlate kernel credit dips with p99 spikes: join kernel_histogram by run_id and timestamp window.
